title: Statistical process control charts for post-deployment safety drift monitoring

original_idea.body:
# Statistical process control charts for post-deployment safety drift monitoring

**Problem:** Post-deployment safety monitoring is a near-empty open-source space; deployers have no simple tool to detect when a model (or a model update) starts drifting toward more harmful or sycophantic behavior over time.

**Direction:** Import Statistical Process Control (Shewhart and EWMA control charts) from manufacturing quality control. Treat a streaming safety metric (refusal rate on a fixed canary prompt set, sycophancy score) as a process to monitor; compute control limits from a baseline window and flag out-of-control points as drift. Simulate a deployment stream with an injected model swap and show the chart catches the regime change with controlled false-alarm rate.

**Why it matters:** Delivers a concrete, reusable open-source post-deployment monitoring prototype — explicitly flagged as a missing infrastructure gap. Decades-proven, lightweight, needs no internal infra; ideal counterfactual-value safety tooling.

**Relevant context:** SPC is standard (Shewhart, Montgomery). Landscape lists post-deployment monitoring as an under-researched gap with no open-source tools. Source subfield: statistical process control / manufacturing QC. Target subfield: ai_control, evaluations_benchmarks.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain: drift monitoring helps catch safety regressions, but a simulated swap's link to catastrophic risk is indirect.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Accessible: canary metrics plus standard SPC charts are simple and beginner-feasible.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused prototype (control chart catching an injected swap), few dependencies.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Neglected infrastructure gap with no open-source tools; needs no internal infra, ideal external work.

low_compute.reasoning: Lightweight metric streaming plus chart math, near CPU-feasible.

novelty.reasoning: SPC is standard and drift-monitoring discussed; the open-source safety-drift prototype may be partly open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: SPC mature; safety-drift application plausibly partly open as tooling.
